outlooks.summary: Threat for strong to severe storms capable of mainly large hail and damaging wind gusts, but possibly a couple of tornadoes, is expected this afternoon and tonight over a portion of the southern Plains and lower Mississippi Valley.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: A low-amplitude western ridge/eastern trough upper flow configuration across the U.S. is forecast to gradually amplify today/tonight, as a southern Plains short-wave trough shifts east across the lower Mississippi Valley into the central Gulf Coast states. With the advance of this short-wave feature contributing toward an amplification of eastern U.S. cyclonic flow, ridging over the West is also progged to sharpen in advance of an eastern Pacific trough/low that will approach the Pacific Northwest Coast overnight. At the surface, a cold front at the leading edge of a substantial surge of Canadian cold air into the U.S. is forecast to shift southward across the southern Plains and southeast across the Tennessee Valley into the southeastern U.S. and Gulf Coast states with time. By sunrise Saturday morning, expect the front to extend from northern North Carolina west-southwest to coastal Texas. Showers and thunderstorms should increase in coverage along this front early in the day, becoming widespread through the afternoon and into the overnight hours from east Texas to Alabama, accompanied locally by severe-weather risk.

sections.title: Southeast Oklahoma and east Texas eastward to western Alabama
sections.text: Showers and a few thunderstorms are forecast to be ongoing at the start of the period from eastern Oklahoma into Arkansas, and to a lesser degree eastward into the Tennessee Valley area. With time, the advance of the surface cold front will support an increase in convection -- near and to the cool side of the front as it advances slowly southward/southeastward. Eventually, upscale growth of convection into a more linearly organized cluster should occur across southern Arkansas/Louisiana/Mississippi, as some destabilization combined with ample shear supports convective organization. Along with some hail risk, damaging wind gusts can be expected as the organizing band of storms moves southward/southeastward through the afternoon and evening. In addition, veering winds through the lower troposphere may support updraft rotation locally, and thus some risk for a couple of QLCS-type tornadoes within stronger/bowing linear bands. Farther west into East Texas, greater heating is expected, beneath the eastern fringe of a steeper lapse rate plume. outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms with damaging winds, occasional hail, and a few tornadoes, are possible today from parts of north-central/northeast/ east Texas to the lower Mississippi Valley and central Gulf Coast regions.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: In mid/upper levels, broadly cyclonic flow is forecast to persist over most of the country east of the Rockies, while a high-amplitude synoptic-scale ridge extends down the Pacific Coastal states/ provinces from Yukon. A well-defined shortwave trough and embedded mid/upper cyclone were evident in moisture-channel imagery north- northeast of HI and west of CA, between 150-155W. This feature should intensify into a strong cyclone aloft through the period and move east-northeastward toward the coastal Pacific Northwest, making landfall there on day-2. Well downstream, a subtle shortwave trough was apparent over the central/southern High Plains, in the broader- scale cyclonic-flow field. This feature is forecast to proceed east-southeastward, reaching the southernmost Appalachians by 12Z, and phasing with weaker/upstream vorticity maxima to form a positively tilted 500-mb trough from near the TN/NC border to southern LA. At the surface, 11Z analysis showed a cold front from Lower MI across southern portions of IL/MO to central OK, the TX Panhandle, and southern CO, becoming quasistationary in the Rockies across central/northern CO, western WY and the ID/MT border region. sections.title: North-central/northeast/east Texas to lower Mississippi Valley
sections.text: Widely scattered to scattered thunderstorms are evident from eastern OK and parts of northeast TX across AR, in a zone of elevated low-level warm advection, moisture transport and isentropic lift to varying LFCs, north of the marine/warm front. Such development should continue in a sporadic/episodic manner throughout the day, with the approach of the southern High Plains shortwave trough and broad, gradually eastward-shifting, 35-45-kt LLJ. Isolated severe hail will be possible north of the warm front. The best-organized severe threat is expected to develop as convection near and north of the warm front, and near the strengthening cold front, shifts southeastward and encounters increasingly unstable, surface-based effective-inflow parcels representative of the marine sector. Activity should aggregate gradually into a primary QLCS, with elements both forward- propagating southeastward across the Arklatex/Delta regions and backbuilding over portions of north-central/northeast TX. Damaging wind will be the main concern. sections.title: Southern Plains to the lower MS Valley through tonight
sections.text: A remnant lee cyclone now near Wichita Falls will move east-southeastward toward northeast TX and northwest LA by this evening, in advance of a series of low-amplitude mid-upper speed maxima. The moist warm sector, characterized by boundary-layer dewpoints of 65-70 F, will continue to spread northward to a baroclinic zone from the Red River valley of TX/OK across southern AR/northern LA through the afternoon. This southern baroclinic zone will be overtaken from northwest to southeast by a surge of arctic air now moving into the I-44 corridor, and this consolidated cold front will continue southeastward to south central/southeast TX and the lower MS Valley by the end of the period. outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms with damaging winds, occasional hail, and a few tornadoes, are expected this afternoon through tonight from north and central Texas eastward to the lower Mississippi Valley.

sections.title: 20Z Update
sections.text: Overall, the forecast outlined in the previous discussion (appended below) is still anticipated and only very minor changes were needed to the outlook based on frontal position and recent guidance.

sections.title: Central and northern LA into central and southwest MS
sections.text: Warm advection showers and thunderstorms have increased across the area over the past hour or so. Current character of these storms suggests they are elevated but continued destabilization downstream could eventually result in more surface-based development. Given the favorable kinematic profiles, a supercell capable of all severe hazards, including a tornado or two, is possible. More short-term details regarding this area are available in MCD 222.

sections.title: Elsewhere across the southern Plains and lower MS Valley
sections.text: Current surface analysis placed a low just west of ADM with a cold front extending west-southwestward into the TX South Plains and a warm front extending southeastward through northeast LA. A dryline also extends southwestward from the low into the TX Big Bend. The airmass ahead of the dryline and south of the warm front continues to destabilize as modest diurnal heating and moisture advection persists. Recent surface observations reveal mid 60s dewpoints as far north as the Red River with MLCAPE estimated over 2000 J/kg across much of TX. 18Z SHV sounding confirmed the presence of an EML with mid-level lapse rates greater than 8 degree C per km. Given this destabilization and southward/southeastward surging cold front, the development of a strong convective line is still anticipated. Primary severe threat within this line will be damaging wind gusts although embedded tornadoes are also possible. Some hail is also possible, particularly with initial development along the cold front. More favorable thermodynamic environment for very large hail is expected across north-central and central TX this evening. ..Mosier.. 04/06/2018 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1123 AM CDT Fri Apr 06 2018/

outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms capable of producing damaging winds, occasional hail, and a couple of tornadoes, will continue tonight from parts of central and eastern Texas eastward across parts of the lower Mississippi Valley.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.text: Convection continues to congeal/organize linearly across the outlook area, with the exception of parts of central and northeastern Texas and into northwest Louisiana, where isolated/rotating storms persist. Otherwise, as the cold front (and conglomerate outflow) continues to surge southward across Louisiana/Mississippi, the associated linear band of storms will remain capable of producing damaging winds, along with marginal hail. A tornado or two will also remain possible -- primarily confined to rotating elements within the QLCS. Potential for very large hail may persist for a couple of hours across portions of central and northeast Texas, though the southward surge of the cold front should eventually undercut the storms resulting in more linear storm organization. Likewise, a short-term supercell tornado threat appears maximized in the short term over northwest Louisiana with supercells just ahead of the front/main convective band for the next hour or so. ..Goss.. 04/07/2018

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A tornado watch will likely be issued for portions of LA and MS. The potential for tornadoes is greatest with warm-sector development that will gradually intensify and focus primarily from central LA northeast into southwestern MS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Radar mosaic shows deepening showers and a few thunderstorms developing in a zone of warm air advection near a remnant maritime front advancing northeast across the lower MS Valley. To the south of the boundary, middle to upper 60s boundary layer dewpoints are contributing to moderate buoyancy. A veering wind profile is resulting in a looping hodograph structure and as the low-level flow strengthens from the west with time, the hodograph will enlarge and result in 150-200 m2/s2 0-1 km SRH. Given the increasing low-level moisture and strengthening low-level shear within a supercell-supportive environment, several supercells will probably develop and pose a risk for a weak tornado or two. The development of a convective line later this evening will move southeast through the area. Damaging winds and perhaps a brief/weak mesovortex tornado will be possible with this later activity.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: WW issuance is likely late this afternoon into this evening across parts of north and central Texas. Thunderstorms will continue to develop across south-central and southeast Oklahoma, advancing into adjacent north Texas this afternoon, with additional storm development possible along a dryline in north-central to central Texas. These storms will become strong to severe with large hail possible along with damaging winds as the primary threats.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Trends in surface observations through 2030Z showed a dryline mixing eastward through far south-central OK, the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex, and across central TX. Ongoing boundary-layer moistening and further surface heating into the lower 80s this afternoon across the warm sector will support additional destabilization. The special 20Z FTW sounding showed the strong surface heating has boosted instability, with ongoing weakening of inhibition, though some cap remains around 780 mb. This latter factor is limiting more widespread storm development at this time, with greater storm coverage possible into the evening along the southward-advancing cold front. Latest GOES-16 visible imagery showed deeper cu/tcu forming from Carter County, OK to Cooke County, TX near the dryline. Regional radar imagery showed thunderstorms have developed near a surface front extending east from a surface low located southeast of KFSI. A cold front advancing south into southern OK this afternoon will continue to undercut these initial storms, though some hail will be possible. Additional storm development is possible along and east of the equatorward-extending dryline, and the cold front as it eventually moves into north TX, where the environment has become moderately unstable. Given a favorable CAPE/shear parameter space in vicinity and just east of the dryline, hail (some very large) and damaging winds will be the primary threats. However, vertically veering winds suggest a tornado or two cannot be ruled out. Elsewhere, damaging winds and hail will be the main threats as the cold front advances south into north to portions of central TX later this afternoon and evening.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe threat will gradually sag south across ww36. Tornado potential remains greatest with discrete storms south of an evolving squall line.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Early-day elevated storms that developed over eastern OK/AR have aided southward surge to a pronounced boundary that currently extends from central MS...northern LA to north of DFW. Convection has gradually intensified along this corridor with an upward evolving squall line expected to begin surging a bit faster southeast over the next few hours. Large hail has been common with the strongest updrafts, primarily over TX/LA; however, damaging wind threat should increase if the squall line begins to surge southeast. 21z sounding from SHV supports large hail with supercell structures as mid-level lapse rates are on the order of 8 C/km with strong surface-based buoyancy observed. Greatest tornado threat will be with more discrete storms just south of the squall line. ..Darrow.. 04/06/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Mostly a severe hail risk will continue through the mid evening hours across North-central Texas including including the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex and areas to the east, with other storms likely to continue increasing in coverage/intensity in areas along and west of I-35 southward into central Texas. Severe Thunderstorm Watch 37 continues until Midnight CDT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: As of 645pm CDT, a small group of storms including the remnants of earlier significant-hail-producing supercells continue to move east/southeast across the Dallas/Fort Worth Metroplex vicinity and areas to the north and east. Steep lapse rates and favorable deep-layer shear will continue to support supercells capable of large hail, although storms will gradually be undercut by a south/southeastward-advancing strong cold front. Such a trend will tend to curb very large hail potential from north to south as a tendency for storm clustering should occur along the cold front, although severe hail and locally damaging winds remain a possibility. Farther south into central Texas, other storms continue to gradually develop and increase in coverage and intensity along a dryline in areas just west of I-35 roughly 25-50 miles west of Waco and Temple as of 645pm CDT. Semi-discrete supercells capable of very large hail are possible supported by very steep mid-level lapse rates and 2000+ J/kg MLCAPE, especially since these storms will generally have at least an hour or two prior to being undercut by the cold front. ..Guyer.. 04/06/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe threat will spread south of ww36 in the next few hours. New watch will likely be issued by 02z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: East-west squall line is sagging south of the I-20 corridor and is progressing toward the southern portions of ww36 at roughly 25kt. Over the last hour or so there appears to be a gradual evolution toward less pre-squall line supercells, though this threat can not be ruled out. Latest thinking is a linear MCS will be the predominant convective mode and damaging winds should become the primary severe threat, along with some large hail. While a tornado can not be ruled out, given the observed shear/instability, storm mode is becoming less favorable for discrete structures.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Instances of severe hail and locally damaging winds will remain a possibility into late evening from north-central into east-central Texas. Severe Thunderstorm Watch 37 continues until Midnight CDT. Additional parts of east-central Texas are being monitored for the possibility of an additional Severe Thunderstorm Watch issuance.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Earlier semi-discrete storms continue to merge and gradually grow upscale in areas east of I-35 to the southeast of the DFW Metroplex, while earlier supercells across central Texas have waned as capping/inhibition have increased. It appears likely that this trend of linearly organized convection will continue with storms spreading southeastward into additional parts of east-central Texas. Convective mode should considerably curb the potential for large hail magnitudes, with the possibility that locally damaging winds could become a bit more of a concern with activity immediately along the front. Although the need for an additional watch is not particularly certain, convective trends will continue to be monitored given the possibility that at least a few severe thunderstorms could exit Severe Thunderstorm Watch 37 before midnight CDT. ..Guyer.. 04/07/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Gusty winds and some hail threat will spread across northern portions of ww38 over the next few hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Extended line of strong storms is propagating south at roughly 15kt...currently extending from west-central portions of AL, west-southwest across northern portions of ww38 into central TX. This squall line appears to have slowed its forward motion a bit over the last few hours but an expanding precip shield should encourage this MCS to continue its southward motion. Gusty winds are the primary threat; although, MRMS data suggests the most robust updrafts may still produce some hail. ..Darrow.. 04/07/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Lingering severe weather potential, mainly a risk for potentially damaging wind gusts, is generally becoming confined to portions of southwestern and south central Louisiana through 2-4 AM CDT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Intense segment of ongoing larger-scale convective system has taken on an increasing bowing structure in radar reflectivity data, and is now surging southeastward at 35+ kt, toward western/central Louisiana coastal areas. This is being aided by strong southeasterly inflow emanating from a moist and potentially unstable boundary layer. During the next hour or two, the strength of this inflow may begin to weaken, as models suggest that the stronger low-level jet will begin to shift east of the Mississippi River with the primary weak frontal wave. However, as convection continues to progress into an increasingly moist boundary layer, associated instability may maintain strength into coastal areas through 08-09Z, accompanied by a risk for potentially damaging wind gusts. ..Kerr.. 04/07/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A new severe weather watch issuance is not expected, but remaining valid portions of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 38 may locally be extended for an hour or two.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Considerable weakening of thunderstorm activity has occurred during the past hour or so, as the primary, weak frontal wave continues to progress well east of the region (into/across the Alabama and Georgia piedmont). Strongest lingering convective development near Baton Rouge is occurring just ahead of a remnant mesoscale convective vortex, in the vicinity of a boundary intersection associated with the conglomerate convective outflow. As this spreads across the Lake Pontchartrain vicinity and nearby coastal areas to the east through daybreak, additional strong storm development may still be possible, with perhaps some risk for hail and strong wind gusts. In general, though, severe weather potential is expected to continue to become increasingly negligible. ..Kerr.. 04/07/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...
